answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware remote attestation. Before an agent can wander into open markets, it submits a cryptographic quote from a security module no larger than a walnut proving its key stays within an isolated island of silicon. Verifiers check quotes against vendor certificates, forcing attackers to incur the verifiable cost of buying physical chips per identity. However, leaked vendor signing keys or firmware exploits let adversaries forge extra identities.
